thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-di:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert
space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Let
$H^{\otimes 0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes 1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(n+1)}:=H^{\otimes n}\widehat\otimes H$ be the completed tensor
powers with elementary tensors $u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); for $n\ge 1$ let
$P_+^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ be the symmetric projection of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] and set
$P_+^{(0)}:=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}$. Write $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ for
its range and define

$$F(H):=\Bigl\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}:\ \psi_n\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\ \text{for all }n,\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$

Then:

(a) for $\psi,\varphi\in F(H)$ the scalar series
$\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle$ converges absolutely and
defines a sesquilinear form, linear in the first argument, with respect to
which $F(H)$ is a complex vector space with inner product
$\langle\psi,\varphi\rangle:=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle$
([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]],
[[def-series-and-absolute-convergence-in-a-normed-space]]);

(b) $(F(H),\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ is a Hilbert space, i.e. the induced norm
is complete ([[def-hilbert-space]]);

(c) the vacuum vector $\Omega:=(1,0,0,\dots)$ satisfies $\|\Omega\|=1$, and the
finite-particle space
$F_0:=\{\psi\in F(H):\psi_n=0\ \text{for all but finitely many }n\}$ is a dense
linear subspace of $F(H)$ ([[def-dense-top]]);

(d) for every $n$ the map
$\iota_n:\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\to F(H)$,
$\iota_n(u):=(0,\dots,0,u,0,\dots)$ (entry in coordinate $n$) is a linear
isometry of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ onto the closed subspace of vectors
supported in coordinate $n$;

(e) if $H$ admits a countable complete orthonormal family
$(e_i)_{i\in I}$, $I$ at most countable
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
then $F(H)$ is separable ([[def-separable-space]]);

(f) *direct sums of self-adjoint operators*: if for every $n\ge 1$ a self-adjoint
operator $T_n$ on the Hilbert space $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with domain
$D(T_n)\subseteq\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ is given
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-unbounded-linear-operator-domain-and-graph]]), and

$$D(T):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \psi_n\in D(T_n)\ \text{for all }n,\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (T\psi)_n:=T_n\psi_n,$$

then $T$ is self-adjoint and $D(T)$ is dense; if in addition every $T_n$ is
bounded with $\sup_{n}\|T_n\|<\infty$, then $T$ is bounded with
$\|T\|=\sup_n\|T_n\|$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

No physical interpretation of $F(H)$, of the tensor powers or of the direct-sum
operators is asserted.
lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-secto:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$ and symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], so that
$$F(H)=\Bigl\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}:\ \psi_n\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)},\ \sum_n\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}$$
is a Hilbert space. For $n\in\mathbb N$ define
$$\Pi_n:F(H)\to F(H),\qquad \Pi_n\psi:=(0,\dots,0,\psi_n,0,\dots)$$
(the entry $\psi_n$ in coordinate $n$ and $0$ in all other coordinates). Then:

(a) each $\Pi_n$ is a bounded linear operator with
$\|\Pi_n\psi\|=\|\psi_n\|$ and $\|\Pi_n\|\le1$; it satisfies
$\Pi_n^2=\Pi_n$, $\Pi_n^*=\Pi_n$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]), and
$\Pi_n$ is the Hilbert orthogonal projection of $F(H)$ onto the closed subspace
$\iota_n(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)})$ of vectors supported in coordinate $n$
([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(b) $\Pi_n\Pi_m=0$ for $n\ne m$, so the ranges are pairwise orthogonal and
$\|\Pi_n\|=1$ whenever $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\ne\{0\}$ (which holds for
every $n$ when $H\ne\{0\}$);

(c) for every $\psi\in F(H)$ the series $\sum_{n}\Pi_n\psi$ converges in norm to
$\psi$, the expansion is orthogonal,
$$\psi=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\Pi_n\psi,\qquad \|\psi\|^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|\Pi_n\psi\|^2,$$
and the partial sums $\sum_{n\le N}\Pi_n$ converge to the identity in the strong
operator topology, i.e. $\bigl\|\psi-\sum_{n\le N}\Pi_n\psi\bigr\|\to0$ for
every $\psi\in F(H)$ ([[def-dense-top]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

(d) $\Pi_n=0$ as an operator if and only if
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\{0\}$; for $H\ne\{0\}$ no $\Pi_n$ vanishes.

No physical interpretation of the Fock space or of its sectors is asserted.
lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-c:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), with
completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$,
Fock space $F(H)$ and finite-particle space $F_0$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] and
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]].

(a) *Contraction map.* For every $f\in H$ and $n\ge0$ there is a unique bounded
linear map $\Psi_f^{(n)}:H^{\otimes(n+1)}\to H^{\otimes n}$ with
$$\langle\varphi,\Psi_f^{(n)}\chi\rangle=\langle f\otimes\varphi,\chi\rangle \qquad(\varphi\in H^{\otimes n},\ \chi\in H^{\otimes(n+1)})$$
([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]); it satisfies
$\|\Psi_f^{(n)}\|\le\|f\|$,
$\Psi_f^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{n+1})=\langle u_1,f\rangle\,u_2\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{n+1}$
on elementary tensors, $\Psi_f^{(n)}(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n+1)})\subseteq\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$,
and the map $f\mapsto\Psi_f^{(n)}$ is conjugate-linear.

(b) *Creation and annihilation on the core.* Define, for $f\in H$ and
$\psi\in F_0$,
$$(S_+(f)\psi)_n:=\sqrt n\,P_+^{(n)}(f\otimes\psi_{n-1})\ (n\ge1),\quad (S_+(f)\psi)_0:=0,$$
$$(S_-(f)\psi)_n:=\sqrt{n+1}\,\Psi_f^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1})\ (n\ge0).$$
Then $S_+(f)\psi,S_-(f)\psi\in F_0$; $S_+(f)$ is linear in $f$ and
$S_-(f)$ is conjugate-linear in $f$; and with
$\|\psi\|_1^2:=\sum_{n}\bigl(n+1\bigr)\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty$ for $\psi\in F_0$,
$$\|S_+(f)\psi\|\le\|f\|\,\|\psi\|_1,\qquad \|S_-(f)\psi\|\le\|f\|\,\|\psi\|_1.$$

(c) *Adjoint relation.* $\langle S_+(f)\varphi,\psi\rangle=\langle\varphi,S_-(f)\psi\rangle$
for all $f\in H$ and $\varphi,\psi\in F_0$
([[def-operator-norm]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

(d) *Canonical commutation relation.* For all $f,g\in H$ and $\psi\in F_0$,
$$S_-(f)S_+(g)\psi-S_+(g)S_-(f)\psi=\langle g,f\rangle\,\psi,$$
and consequently
$$\|S_+(g)\psi\|^2=\|S_-(g)\psi\|^2+\|g\|^2\|\psi\|^2.$$

Neither $S_+(f)$ nor $S_-(f)$ is asserted to be bounded on $F(H)$, and no
physical interpretation (particle creation, radiation or measurement) is
asserted.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adj:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, contraction maps
$\Psi_f^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$ and core operators $S_\pm(f)$ on the
finite-particle space $F_0$ as in
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]]. For $f\in H$
define
$$D(A_+(f)):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}(n+1)\bigl\|P_+^{(n+1)}(f\otimes\psi_n)\bigr\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (A_+(f)\psi)_n:=\sqrt n\,P_+^{(n)}(f\otimes\psi_{n-1})\ (n\ge1),\ (A_+(f)\psi)_0:=0,$$
$$D(A_-(f)):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}(n+1)\bigl\|\Psi_f^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1})\bigr\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (A_-(f)\psi)_n:=\sqrt{n+1}\,\Psi_f^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1}).$$
Put $D_1:=\{\psi\in F(H):\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$. Then:

(a) $A_+(f)$ and $A_-(f)$ are well-defined linear operators on $F(H)$ with the
displayed domains, and they are the closure and the adjoint of the core operator:
$$A_+(f)=\overline{S_+(f)}=S_-(f)^*,\qquad A_-(f)=S_+(f)^*=\overline{S_-(f)}$$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(b) both $A_\pm(f)$ are closed, densely defined and satisfy
$A_+(f)^*=A_-(f)$, $A_-(f)^*=A_+(f)$; in particular $F_0\subseteq D_1\subseteq D(A_\pm(f))$;

(c) for every $\psi\in D_1$, $\|A_+(f)\psi\|\le\|f\|\,\|\psi\|_1$ and
$\|A_-(f)\psi\|\le\|f\|\,\|\psi\|_1$, where
$\|\psi\|_1^2=\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2$;

(d) for every $g\in H$ and $\psi\in D_1$ the identity
$$\|A_+(g)\psi\|^2=\|A_-(g)\psi\|^2+\|g\|^2\|\psi\|^2$$
holds.

No boundedness of $A_\pm(f)$ on $F(H)$, no self-adjointness of $A_\pm(f)$, and
no physical interpretation is asserted.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-ope:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric
projections $P_+^{(n)}$ and Fock space $F(H)$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]. Define the
number operator by
$$D(N):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (N\psi)_n:=n\psi_n .$$
Then:

(a) $N$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $F(H)$ with the displayed
domain; $N\ge0$ in the sense that $\langle N\psi,\psi\rangle\ge0$ for
$\psi\in D(N)$, $N\Omega=0$, and $F_0$ is a core for $N$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(b) for every $n$, every nonzero $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ satisfies
$N\iota_n(u)=n\,\iota_n(u)$, and for $H\ne\{0\}$ the spectrum of $N$ is
$\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$;

(c) for $f\in H$ and $\psi\in F_0$ the core operators of
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]] satisfy
$$N S_+(f)\psi-S_+(f)N\psi=S_+(f)\psi,\qquad N S_-(f)\psi-S_-(f)N\psi=-S_-(f)\psi ;$$

(d) $D(N)\subseteq D_1:=\{\psi:\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$, and for every
$\psi\in D(N)$,
$$\|N\psi\|^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2,\qquad \langle N\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\|\psi_n\|^2 .$$

No physical interpretation of $N$, and no assertion about particle number
measurement, is made.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+z\overline w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mod:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\omega>0$ and
$\beta>0$ be real parameters, let $F(\mathbb C)$ be the one-mode Fock space
with its complete orthonormal family $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ and number
operator $N$ as in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]]
and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]], and define the
operator $G_\beta\in\mathcal B(F(\mathbb C))$ by
$$G_\beta e_n:=e^{-\beta\omega n}e_n\qquad(n\in\mathbb N)$$
together with bounded linear extension. Then:

(a) $G_\beta$ is a bounded self-adjoint positive operator with $\|G_\beta\|=1$,
and $G_\beta=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb N}e^{-\beta\omega n}\,\mathrm{id}$ on the
Fock sectors ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]);

(b) the series of weights converge,
$$Z(\beta):=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}e^{-\beta\omega n}=\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\omega}},\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\,e^{-\beta\omega n}=\frac{e^{-\beta\omega}}{(1-e^{-\beta\omega})^2};$$

(c) $G_\beta$ is trace class with
$\|G_\beta\|_1=\operatorname{tr}G_\beta=Z(\beta)$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);

(d) $\rho_\beta:=G_\beta/Z(\beta)$ is a density operator on $F(\mathbb C)$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]), and its
number expectation, defined by the absolutely convergent spectral sum
$\langle N\rangle_\beta:=\sum_{n}n\,e^{-\beta\omega n}/Z(\beta)$, equals
$$\langle N\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\omega}}{1-e^{-\beta\omega}}=\frac1{e^{\beta\omega}-1};$$
more generally $\sum_nn^k e^{-\beta\omega n}<\infty$ for every $k\ge1$.

The parameter $\beta$ is a positive real parameter of the model; its
identification with an inverse temperature, and the interpretation of
$\rho_\beta$ as a physical thermal state, are additional physical assumptions
not asserted here.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with a countable complete orthonormal family $(e_j)_{j\ge1}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$, let $\beta>0$, and let
$F(H)$ be the Fock space of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]. Let
$\mathcal M$ be the set of finite nondecreasing sequences
$I=(j_1\le\cdots\le j_n)$ with $n\ge0$ (the empty sequence included); for
$I=(j_1\le\cdots\le j_n)$ put
$$v_I:=P_+^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})\in F(H)\quad(n\ge1),\qquad v_{\varnothing}:=\Omega,\qquad \lambda_I:=\varepsilon_{j_1}+\cdots+\varepsilon_{j_n}\ (\text{empty sum }0),$$
and $u_I:=v_I/\|v_I\|$. Then:

(a) $(u_I)_{I\in\mathcal M}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(H)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]);

(b) the diagonal operator
$$D(D_\beta):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-2\beta\lambda_I}|\langle\psi,u_I\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad D_\beta\psi:=\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}\langle\psi,u_I\rangle u_I$$
is bounded, self-adjoint and positive with $\|D_\beta\|\le1$; it is trace class
exactly when $\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}<\infty$, and then
$\operatorname{tr}D_\beta=\sum_Ie^{-\beta\lambda_I}$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);

(c) for every $N\ge1$, $\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{I\in\mathcal M\\ I\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}}}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\prod_{j=1}^N\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}$, and
$$\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\lim_{N\to\infty}\prod_{j=1}^N\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}\in(0,\infty];$$

(d) *product criterion*: $\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}<\infty$ if and only if
$\sum_{j\ge1}e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$, and in that case
$$\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\prod_{j=1}^\infty\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}<\infty ;$$

(e) consequently $D_\beta$ is trace class if and only if
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$, with the trace given by the infinite
product in (d).

The operator $D_\beta$ is a purely mathematical diagonal operator on $F(H)$;
no thermal, thermodynamic or measurement interpretation is asserted.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fermion-an:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\beta>0$ and let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$ and
$\mu\in\mathbb R$ be real data; write $q_j:=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)}$.

(a) *Single fermionic orbital.* On $\mathfrak h:=\mathbb C^2$ with orthonormal
basis $(u_0,u_1)$ define the bounded self-adjoint operator $N_-$ by
$N_-u_0=0$, $N_-u_1=u_1$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Then the diagonal
operator $F:=\sum_{k=0}^1e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}\,T_{u_k,u_k}$ is
positive, self-adjoint, finite rank, and
$$\operatorname{tr}F=1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)},\qquad \frac{\sum_{k=0}^1k\,e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}}{\operatorname{tr}F}=\frac1{e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1}$$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]],
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(b) *Countable grand-canonical factor products.* Define
$\mathcal N:=\{N\subseteq\{1,2,\dots\}:N\text{ finite}\}$ and set
$$Z_{\mathrm B}:=\sup_{N\in\mathcal N}\ \prod_{j\in N}\frac1{1-q_j}\in(0,\infty],\qquad Z_{\mathrm F}:=\sup_{N\in\mathcal N}\ \prod_{j\in N}(1+q_j)\in[1,\infty],$$
with the convention $Z_{\mathrm B}:=+\infty$ if some $j$ has
$\varepsilon_j-\mu\le0$. Then:
$$Z_{\mathrm B}<\infty\iff\sum_j e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty \ \text{ and }\ \mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j,\qquad Z_{\mathrm F}<\infty\iff\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty,$$
and in these finite cases $Z_{\mathrm B}=\prod_{j\ge1}(1-q_j)^{-1}$ and
$Z_{\mathrm F}=\prod_{j\ge1}(1+q_j)$.

(c) *Mode occupancies and dilute remainders.* For a single mode with
$0<q<1$ (boson) and $q>0$ (fermion),
$$\frac{\sum_{n\ge0}n\,q^n}{\sum_{n\ge0}q^n}=\frac q{1-q}=q+\frac{q^2}{1-q},\qquad \frac{\sum_{n=0}^1n\,q^n}{\sum_{n=0}^1q^n}=\frac q{1+q}=q-\frac{q^2}{1+q};$$
consequently the deviations from $q$ are bounded by $q^2/(1-q)$ and
$q^2/(1+q)$ respectively, and both are at most $2q^2$ when $q\le1/2$.

All statements are mathematical statements about diagonal weights and products;
no identification of $\beta,\mu,\varepsilon_j$ with physical temperatures,
chemical potentials or energies, and no thermal or thermodynamic conclusion,
is asserted.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gib:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak H$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space of dimension
$d\ge1$ with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $H:\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$ be a self-adjoint
linear operator with real eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_d$ (repeated according to
multiplicity) and orthonormal eigenbasis $(v_1,\dots,v_d)$, and let $\beta>0$.
Write
$$Z:=\sum_{j=1}^d e^{-\beta E_j}\in(0,\infty),\qquad \rho_\beta:=\frac1Z\sum_{j=1}^d e^{-\beta E_j}T_{v_j,v_j},$$
where $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). Let
$\mathcal D$ be the set of density operators on $\mathfrak H$, i.e. positive
self-adjoint trace-class operators $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]), and
for $\rho\in\mathcal D$ with eigenvalues $w_1,\dots,w_d\ge0$ (counted with
multiplicity and in any order) define the entropy
$$s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i\in[0,\log d]$$
([[def-natural-logarithm]]). Then:

(a) $\rho_\beta\in\mathcal D$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\frac1Z\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}E_j$,
and
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z ;$$

(b) for every $\rho\in\mathcal D$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)\ \ge\ -\beta^{-1}\log Z ;$$

(c) for every $\rho\in\mathcal D$, $s(\rho)\le\log d$, with $s(\rho)=\log d$ if
and only if $\rho=d^{-1}\,\mathrm{id}$; when $H=0$ one has $Z=d$,
$\rho_\beta=d^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ and the bound in (b) is attained there.

The combination $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)$ is a purely
mathematical functional of $(\rho,H,\beta)$; identifying $\beta$ with an
inverse physical temperature and $\rho_\beta$ with a thermal equilibrium state
are additional physical assumptions not asserted here.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-variationa:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a self-adjoint
operator on a nonzero complex Hilbert space $\mathfrak H$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]) which is bounded below, let
$E_0:=\inf\sigma(H)\in\mathbb R$, let $E$ be the projection-valued measure of
$H$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), put $P:=E(\{E_0\})$, and assume that
$g>0$ is a spectral gap:
$$\sigma(H)\cap(E_0,E_0+g)=\varnothing .$$
For $u\in D(|H|^{1/2})$ write $E_u(B):=\langle E(B)u,u\rangle$ for Borel sets
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]) and put
$q_H[u]:=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_u(\lambda)$; by
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] (c) this
integral exists for $u\in D(|H|^{1/2})$, and for $u\in D(H)$ it equals
$\langle Hu,u\rangle$. Then for every $u\in D(|H|^{1/2})$ with $\|u\|=1$:

(a) $q_H[u]-E_0=\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R}(\lambda-E_0)\,dE_u(\lambda)\ \ge\ g\,\|(I-P)u\|^2$;

(b) if $q_H[u]\le E_0+\varepsilon$ for some $\varepsilon\ge0$, then
$\|(I-P)u\|^2\le\varepsilon/g$; in particular, if $\varepsilon<g$ then $Pu\ne0$.

No claim is made about the existence of a ground eigenvector, about $E_0$
being an eigenvalue, or about any physical interpretation of the trial vector.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fi:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $N\ge1$, let
$m_1,\dots,m_N>0$ and $\hbar>0$, write points of $\mathbb R^{3N}$ as
$X=(x_1,\dots,x_N)$ with $x_i\in\mathbb R^3$, and let $\mathcal F_2$ be the
Plancherel transform of [[thm-plancherel]] with the convention
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(X)e^{-2\pi iX\cdot\xi}\,dX$ on $L^1$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]]). Define the quadratic weight and the
free kinetic operator
$$\kappa(\xi_1,\dots,\xi_N):=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{\hbar^2}{2m_i}|\xi_i|^2,\qquad K:=\mathcal F_2^*\,M_\kappa\,\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(K):=\{u\in L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C):\ \kappa\,\mathcal F_2u\in L^2\}$$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]).
Let $V:\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and bounded, with
$\|V\|_\infty:=\operatorname{ess\,sup}|V|<\infty$, and let $M_V$ be
multiplication by $V$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]). Then:

(a) $K$ is a self-adjoint positive operator with domain $D(K)$, and $D(K)$ is
the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$ as a set, with
$\|\cdot\|_{W^{2,2}}$ equivalent to the graph norm
$u\mapsto(\|u\|^2+\|Ku\|^2)^{1/2}$
([[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]);

(b) $H:=K+M_V$ with $D(H):=D(K)$ is self-adjoint and bounded below by
$-\|V\|_\infty$; the space $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$ is a core for
both $K$ and $H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]],
[[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]);

(c) for every $r\ge1$ the operator $K\otimes I_r+M_V\otimes I_r$ on
$L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)\otimes\mathbb C^r$, with domain
$D(K)\otimes\mathbb C^r$, is self-adjoint and bounded below by $-\|V\|_\infty$.

In particular, if $V_i:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ and $W_{ij}:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$
($1\le i<j\le N$) are measurable and bounded and
$V(X):=\sum_iV_i(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W_{ij}(x_i-x_j)$, then $\|V\|_\infty\le\sum_i\|V_i\|_\infty+\sum_{i<j}\|W_{ij}\|_\infty<\infty$
and (a)-(c) apply. No Hunziker-van Winter-Zhislin threshold statement, no
stability of matter, no thermodynamic-limit and no physical interpretation is
asserted.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutatio:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak H$ be a complex Hilbert space, let $H$ be a self-adjoint operator on
$\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]),
let $N\ge1$, and let $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_N}$ be unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$
with $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$ and $U_\pi^*=U_{\pi^{-1}}$ for all
$\pi,\sigma\in S_N$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]). Define
$$P_+:=\frac1{N!}\sum_{\pi\in S_N}U_\pi,\qquad P_-:=\frac1{N!}\sum_{\pi\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)U_\pi .$$
Assume that for every $\pi\in S_N$,
$$U_\pi D(H)\subseteq D(H)\qquad\text{and}\qquad U_\pi H\psi=HU_\pi\psi\quad(\psi\in D(H)).$$
Then:

(a) $P_+$ and $P_-$ are orthogonal projections on $\mathfrak H$;

(b) for every $z\in\rho(H)$ one has
$U_\pi(H-z)^{-1}=(H-z)^{-1}U_\pi$ and hence $P_\pm(H-z)^{-1}=(H-z)^{-1}P_\pm$;

(c) $P_\pm D(H)\subseteq D(H)$ and $HP_\pm\psi=P_\pm H\psi$ for every
$\psi\in D(H)$;

(d) if $\operatorname{ran}P_\pm\ne\{0\}$, then the restriction
$H_\pm:=H|_{D(H)\cap\operatorname{ran}P_\pm}$ is a self-adjoint operator on the
Hilbert space $\operatorname{ran}P_\pm$
([[thm-self-adjointness-range-criterion]]);

(e) *application*: let $N\ge1$, $m>0$, $\hbar>0$, let $r\ge1$, let
$V_{\mathrm{ext}},W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and bounded, put
$V(X):=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W(x_i-x_j)$ on
$\mathbb R^{3N}$, let $K$ be the free kinetic operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] with all masses
$m_i=m$, let $\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)^{\otimes N}\to L^2(\mathbb R^{3N})$ be
the iterated Euclidean product unitary
([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), let $U_\pi$ be the
permutation unitaries of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]
and set
$$U_\pi^{\mathrm{phys}}:=\Theta\,U_\pi\,\Theta^{-1},\qquad P_\pm^{\mathrm{phys}}:=\Theta\,P_\pm^{(N)}\,\Theta^{-1}.$$
Then $H:=K+M_V$ satisfies the hypotheses above for the representation
$U_\pi^{\mathrm{phys}}$, so $P_\pm^{\mathrm{phys}}$ reduce $H$ and the
restrictions of $H$ to the symmetric and antisymmetric sectors are self-adjoint
on those sectors.

No spin-statistics statement, no identification of a physical species with a
sector, and no claim about bound states or spectra is made.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-co:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $N\ge1$ and $r\ge1$,
let $m_1,\dots,m_N>0$, $\hbar>0$, let $a_1,\dots,a_M\in\mathbb R^3$ be fixed
points, and let $z_{im},z_{ij}\in\mathbb R$ be real coefficients
($1\le i\le N$, $1\le m\le M$, $1\le i<j\le N$). Let $K$ be the free kinetic
operator of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]],
$D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$ with equivalent graph norm, and define
the singular multiplier
$$V(X):=\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{m=1}^M\frac{z_{im}}{|x_i-a_m|}+\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}\frac{z_{ij}}{|x_i-x_j|},\qquad X=(x_1,\dots,x_N)\in\mathbb R^{3N},$$
as an a.e.-defined real measurable function
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). Then:

(a) each of the multipliers $u\mapsto u/|x_i-a_m|$ and
$u\mapsto u/|x_i-x_j|$ is $K$-bounded with $K$-bound zero: for every
$\eta>0$ there is a finite constant $C_\eta$ with
$$\Bigl\|\frac{u}{|x_i-a_m|}\Bigr\|_2\le\eta\|Ku\|_2+C_\eta\|u\|_2,\qquad \Bigl\|\frac{u}{|x_i-x_j|}\Bigr\|_2\le\eta\|Ku\|_2+C_\eta\|u\|_2$$
for all $u\in D(K)$ ([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]],
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]);

(b) $D(K)\subseteq D(M_V)$, and $M_V$ is symmetric on $D(K)$ with $K$-bound
zero; consequently
$$H:=K+M_V,\qquad D(H):=D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C),$$
is self-adjoint and bounded below, and $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$
is a core for $H$ ([[thm-kato-rellich]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(c) the operator $K\otimes I_r+M_V\otimes I_r$ on
$L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)\otimes\mathbb C^r$ with domain $D(K)\otimes\mathbb C^r$
is self-adjoint and bounded below;

(d) if $m_1=\cdots=m_N=m$ and the coefficients are permutation invariant
($z_{im}$ independent of $i$ and $z_{ij}$ independent of the pair), then the
transported permutation unitaries of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]]
reduce $H$, and the restrictions of $H$ to the symmetric and antisymmetric
sectors are self-adjoint on those sectors.

No Hunziker-van Winter-Zhislin threshold statement, no uniform-in-$N$
stability, no thermodynamic limit, no spectral statement beyond
self-adjointness and boundedness from below, and no physical interpretation of
$H$, the masses or the coefficients is asserted.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the Axiom of Dependent Choice and the
Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a parameter $\alpha>0$, define the transverse
subspace
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for a.e. }k\Bigr\}$$
with the $L^2$ inner product, define the bounded multiplier-valued function
$\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$ and $\Pi(0):=0$, and let
$M_\Pi$ be multiplication by $\Pi$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Write
$\varepsilon(k):=\alpha|k|$ and let $M_\varepsilon$ be multiplication by
$\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}:=M_\varepsilon|_{\mathfrak h}$.
Let $F(\mathfrak h)$ be the Fock space of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] with sectors
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and for $n\ge1$ define
$$T_n\psi:=\varepsilon_n\psi,\quad \varepsilon_n(k_1,\dots,k_n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha|k_i|,\qquad D(T_n):=\{\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}:\varepsilon_n\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\},$$
and $T_0:=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Finally put
$$H_f:=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_n,\qquad D(H_f):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(\mathfrak h):\ \sum_n\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$
Then:

(a) $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ is a closed separable subspace of
$L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$, invariant under $M_\varepsilon$, and
$\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on
$\mathfrak h$ with $D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\varepsilon f\in\mathfrak h\}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(b) each $T_n$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with the displayed domain
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]);

(c) $H_f$ is self-adjoint and positive with domain $D(H_f)$; it commutes with
every sector projection $\Pi_n$ (i.e. $T_n$ maps its sector into itself);

(d) for every $\beta>0$ the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]) is not compact and in particular not trace
class ([[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]); more
precisely its restriction to the one-particle sector equals the multiplication
operator $M_{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}$ on $\mathfrak h$, which is not compact, and
the restriction of a compact operator to a closed invariant subspace is compact.

The identification of $\mathfrak h$, $\varepsilon$ and $H_f$ with physical
transverse photons in a chosen frame is a separate model assumption and is not
asserted here; no thermal interpretation of $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is claimed either.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-dir:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$ and symmetric
projections $P_\pm^{(n)}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]). Then:

(a) *Slater vectors*: for $n\ge2$ and orthonormal $u_1,\dots,u_n\in H$, the
Slater vector
$$S(u_1,\dots,u_n):=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\,u_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{\sigma(n)}$$
satisfies $\|S(u_1,\dots,u_n)\|=1$ and
$S(u_1,\dots,u_n)=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)$;

(b) *exclusion*: if $u_i=u_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then
$P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)=0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] (d));

(c) *two orbitals, bounded pair interaction*: let $u,v\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
be normalized and orthogonal, let $W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and
bounded with $W(-z)=W(z)$ for a.e. $z$, let
$\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3)\to L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ be the
Euclidean product unitary
([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]), put
$\varphi_\pm:=(u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u)/\sqrt2$ and
$$D:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}|u(x)|^2|v(y)|^2W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,\qquad X:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}\overline{u(x)}v(x)u(y)\overline{v(y)}\,W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,$$
integrals of absolutely integrable functions. Then $D,X\in\mathbb R$ and the
pair expectation of the multiplier $M_W$ in the two spatial states is
$$\bigl\langle M_W(\Theta\varphi_\pm),\Theta\varphi_\pm\bigr\rangle=D\pm X .$$

(d) *repulsive Coulomb exchange*: let $\kappa>0$, $W(z)=\kappa/|z|$, let
$u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\cap L^2$ be normalized and orthogonal
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
The vectors $\Theta\varphi_\pm$ belong to $D(M_W)$: Hardy translated in the $y$ variable and Tonelli give $\iint|u(x)v(y)|^2/|x-y|^2\le4\|u\|_2^2\|\nabla v\|_2^2<\infty$, and the swapped product has the same property. Then the integrals $D$ and $X$ converge absolutely, $0\le D<\infty$,
$X\in\mathbb R$ with $X\ge0$; consequently
$D-X\le D+X$, i.e. the antisymmetric spatial pair state has the lower
expectation of the repulsive Coulomb pair interaction.

The exchange calculation is a statement about the indicated spatial vectors; it
does not deduce the spin-statistics assignment of any species, and combining the
spatial states with spin requires a separately stipulated symmetry rule. No
physical interpretation of $D$, $X$ or the states is asserted.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dip:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\alpha>0$, let
$\mathfrak h$ be the transverse space and $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$ the free
transverse Fock Hamiltonian of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
and let $A_\pm(g)$, $g\in\mathfrak h$, be the maximal creation and annihilation
operators on $F(\mathfrak h)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]]. Fix a cutoff
$\Lambda>0$ and vectors $g_1,\dots,g_J\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\}\quad\text{and}\quad \frac{g_j}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h,\qquad \varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|,$$
and define the symmetric operator
$$\phi(g):=A_-(g)+A_+(g),\qquad D(\phi(g)):=D(H_f).$$
Let $d\ge1$, let $H_a$ be a Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix, and let
$D_1,\dots,D_J$ be Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices with operator norms
$\|D_j\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]). Then:

(a) for every $\Psi\in D(H_f)$,
$$\|A_-(g)\Psi\|^2\le\Bigl\|\frac g{\sqrt\varepsilon}\Bigr\|^2\langle H_f\Psi,\Psi\rangle,\qquad \|A_+(g)\Psi\|^2=\|A_-(g)\Psi\|^2+\|g\|^2\|\Psi\|^2;$$
in particular $\Psi\in D(A_+(g))\cap D(A_-(g))$ and for every $\eta>0$ there is
a finite $C_\eta$ with
$$\|\phi(g)\Psi\|\le\eta\|H_f\Psi\|+C_\eta\|\Psi\| ;$$

(b) $\phi(g)$ is symmetric on $D(H_f)$ and has $H_f$-bound zero
([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(c) the free part $H_0:=H_a\otimes I+I\otimes H_f$ with domain
$C^d\otimes D(H_f)$ is self-adjoint on $\mathbb C^d\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]); for every $\eta_0\in\mathbb R$ the operator
$$H:=H_0+\eta_0\sum_{j=1}^JD_j\otimes\phi(g_j),\qquad D(H):=C^d\otimes D(H_f),$$
is self-adjoint on $\mathbb C^d\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$ and bounded below
([[thm-kato-rellich]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] (c)).

The product $D_j\otimes\phi(g_j)$ and the coupling $\eta_0$ carry the dimension
of energy in a physical normalisation; this normalisation is a model choice and
no physical statement about radiation or spontaneous emission is made here.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-vacuum-emi:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Adopt the objects and
hypotheses of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]]:
$d\ge1$, Hermitian matrices $H_a,D_1,\dots,D_J$ on $\mathbb C^d$, cutoff
$\Lambda>0$, transverse vectors $g_j$ with
$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{0<\varepsilon\le\Lambda\}$ and
$g_j/\sqrt\varepsilon\in\mathfrak h$, coupling $\eta_0\in\mathbb R$,
$$H_0:=H_a\otimes I+I\otimes H_f,\qquad B:=\eta_0\sum_{j=1}^JD_j\otimes\phi(g_j),\qquad H:=H_0+B,$$
all with domain $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$ so that $H_0$ and $H$ are self-adjoint on
that domain. Fix $\hbar>0$, a unit vector $v_a\in\mathbb C^d$ and
$\Psi_0:=v_a\otimes\Omega$, and define the interaction-picture family
$$V(t):=e^{itH_0/\hbar}Be^{-itH_0/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
For $n\ge0$ and $t\ge0$ let
$$\Psi_n(t):=\Bigl(\frac1{i\hbar}\Bigr)^{\!n}\int_{0<t_1<\cdots<t_n<t}V(t_n)\cdots V(t_1)\Psi_0\,dt_1\cdots dt_n$$
(iterated Bochner integral in $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$; $\Psi_0(t):=\Psi_0$). Put
$C:=2\sum_{j=1}^J\|D_j\|\,\|g_j\|/\hbar$ and $C':=C\Lambda$. Then:

(a) for all $n\ge0$ and $t\ge0$,
$$\|\Psi_n(t)\|\le\frac{(|\eta_0|Ct)^n}{\sqrt{n!}};$$

(b) the vectors $\Psi_n(t)$ lie in $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$, the series
$\sum_{n\ge0}\Psi_n(t)$ converges in the graph norm of $H_f$ uniformly for $t$
in compact subsets of $[0,\infty)$, and its sum $\Psi(t)$ satisfies
$$i\hbar\,\partial_t\Psi(t)=V(t)\Psi(t),\qquad \Psi(0)=\Psi_0 ;$$

(c) the Dyson sum solves the actual self-adjoint evolution:
$e^{-itH_0/\hbar}\Psi(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}\Psi_0$ for every $t\ge0$;

(d) explicit tail bound: for $0\le t\le T$ and $N\ge1$,
$$\Bigl\|e^{-itH/\hbar}\Psi_0-e^{-itH_0/\hbar}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\Psi_n(t)\Bigr\|\le\sum_{n\ge N}\frac{(|\eta_0|CT)^n}{\sqrt{n!}} .$$

The convergence is proved for the actual self-adjoint $H$ on the stated domain;
this is not a formal manipulation of divergent series, and no all-time
weak-coupling, Markov or exponential-decay statement is made.
thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-golden-rul:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\hbar>0$.

**(a) The golden-rule kernel.** For $t>0$ define
$$K_t(x):=\frac1{\hbar^2t}\Bigl|\int_0^te^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^2,\qquad x\in\mathbb R .$$
Then $K_t$ is continuous, nonnegative and even, and for $x\ne0$
$$K_t(x)=\frac{4\sin^2\bigl(xt/(2\hbar)\bigr)}{x^2t},\qquad K_t(0)=\frac t{\hbar^2};$$
moreover for every $\delta>0$ and every $x$ with $|x|\ge\delta$,
$$K_t(x)\le\frac4{x^2t}\le\frac4{\delta^2t},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}.$$

**(b) Approximate identity.** Let $J\in L^1(\mathbb R)$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]) and let $\Delta\in\mathbb R$.
If the representative $J$ is continuous at $\Delta$
([[def-continuity-real]]), then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)J(\Delta+x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}J(\Delta)$$
([[def-limits-at-infinity]]).

**(c) First-order emission coefficient.** Adopt the objects and hypotheses of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]]: $\alpha>0$, the
transverse space $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$, the cutoff $\Lambda>0$, the vectors
$g_1,\dots,g_J\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_j}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h,$$
the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices $H_a,D_1,\dots,D_J$ and the coupling
$\eta_0\in\mathbb R$. Let $v_a,v_b$ be orthonormal eigenvectors of $H_a$ with
$H_av_a=E_av_a$, $H_av_b=E_av_b$, and let $\Delta:=E_a-E_b>0$. Put
$$c_j:=\langle D_jv_a,v_b\rangle\ (\mathbb C^d\text{ inner product}),\qquad M:=\sum_{j=1}^Jc_jg_j\in\mathfrak h,$$
and define the finite Borel measure
$$\nu_b(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf 1_A(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k, \qquad A\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
and for $t\ge0$ the amplitude
$$A_b(k,t):=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}M(k)\int_0^te^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds .$$
Then:

(i) $\nu_b$ is a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb R$ with
$\nu_b(\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda])=0$, and
$$\int_{\mathbb R}f\,d\nu_b=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k$$
for every Borel $f\ge0$;

(ii) $A_b(\cdot,t)\in\mathfrak h$ for every $t\ge0$, and
for $t>0$,
$$\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\eta_0^2t\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_b(E).$$
At $t=0$ the amplitude is zero, so its squared norm is zero; no $K_0$ is used.

(iii) if $\nu_b=J_b\lambda$ for some $J_b\in L^1(\lambda)$ with $J_b=0$
$\lambda$-a.e. on $\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$ and the representative $J_b$
continuous at $\Delta$, then for $0<\Delta<\Lambda$
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac1t\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\frac{2\pi\eta_0^2}{\hbar}J_b(\Delta);$$
if instead $\Delta>\Lambda$, then the same limit exists and equals $0$. The
boundary case $\Delta=\Lambda$ is not asserted.

*Motivation and scope.* In the cutoff dipole model of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] the vector
$A_b(\cdot,t)$ is the explicit single-vertex amplitude with the atom passing
from $v_a$ to $v_b$ and one photon emitted; $\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|^2$ is the
corresponding first-order photon coefficient, and (iii) is the golden-rule
limit of that coefficient divided by $t$. This item computes only the limit of
the explicit coefficient, under the stated hypotheses on the spectral density
$J_b$. It asserts no approximation of the exact model evolution, no all-time or
weak-coupling limit, no Markov property and no exact exponential decay, and it
reports no measurement or empirical rate. The parameter $\hbar$, the coupling
$\eta_0$ and the matrices $D_j$ enter as mathematical normalisation data of the
model; their physical identification is a separate assumption.
